source: OWASP IoTGoat — deliberately insecure OpenWrt-based firmware
verified: 2026-10-03 — every path/string/function below was confirmed against the committed rootfs/ AND the IoTGoat source tree (OWASP/IoTGoat). No VERIFY steps remain.

hardcoded-credentials.challenge: OWASP IoT #1 — Weak, Guessable, or Hardcoded Passwords
hardcoded-credentials.answer_summary: Firmware ships with hardcoded login credentials. /etc/shadow contains MD5 ($1$) password hashes baked into the image, including user 'iotgoatuser' (password '7ujMko0vizxv') and 'root'.
hardcoded-credentials.why_good_for_the_race: Rock-solid ground truth findable by all three strategies: grep ($1$ / iotgoatuser), filesystem-walk (open /etc/shadow), and strings. Recommended default round.

shellback-backdoor.challenge: OWASP IoT #2 — Insecure Network Services (bind-shell backdoor)
shellback-backdoor.answer_summary: A 'shellback' bind-shell backdoor binary is installed at /usr/bin/shellback and auto-started at boot via /etc/init.d/shellback (enabled in /etc/config/shellback). It listens on TCP 5515 and forks a shell to any client.

command-injection.challenge: OWASP IoT #3 — Insecure Ecosystem Interfaces (command injection)
command-injection.answer_summary: A hidden LuCI 'Secret Developer Diagnostics' page (admin/iotgoat/cmdinject) posts to the webcmd handler, which passes the unsanitized 'cmd' form value straight into io.popen() — command injection as root.
